$comment: The sandbox's plugins, in picker order, and the scenarios each demo must be able to play. Read by sandbox.astro, scripts/lint-demos.mjs and the demo browser test. A scenario's state is applied over DEFAULT_STATE in site/src/lib/sandbox.ts.

engagement.note: Every interaction on this page is read from the DOM. Nothing on the site was instrumented.

scenarios.label: A visit, end to end
scenarios.note: Every step is a real interaction on a page. Watch the contact clicks: an email and a phone link report only that a click happened, never the address.

scenarios.label: Links carrying secrets
scenarios.note: Two of these links carry an access token and a signed URL in their query strings. Only the host and path arrive — the query is dropped, not truncated.

scenarios.label: A form with personal data in it
scenarios.note: The newsletter form has a filled email field. Its identity and destination host arrive; no field value does, on start or on submit.

scenarios.label: Cookie banner unanswered
scenarios.note: Pair it with a consent plugin and nothing is sent until the visitor accepts — every interaction is refused, with the reason.

shopify.note: Each step is a Shopify Web Pixels event; the plugin maps it to one Datadog action.

scenarios.label: Happy path
scenarios.note: The normal case: every step maps to one Datadog action. The order arrives once, with its value, tax, shipping and coupon.

scenarios.label: Shopper declines cookies
scenarios.note: Shopify’s consent API says no, so the plugin sends nothing at all — not even the order. Every step is refused, with the reason.

scenarios.label: Thank-you page reloaded
scenarios.note: The last two steps are the same order: a reload. The second is refused, so revenue is not counted twice.

scenarios.label: Card data in the payload
scenarios.note: The payment step’s recorded payload contains a card number and CVV. Look at what arrives: only the payment method name.

woocommerce.note: Cart events come from WooCommerce’s own DOM events; the order comes from the thank-you page.

scenarios.label: Happy path
scenarios.note: Cart events come from WooCommerce’s own DOM events; the order comes from the thank-you page. Note the card number and billing address in the payload never arrive.

scenarios.label: Cookie banner unanswered
scenarios.note: Nothing is sent, not even the customer ID, and RUM itself is held at not-granted. Pending events are dropped rather than queued, so accepting later does not backfill them.

scenarios.label: Send the email address
scenarios.note: Opted in, the email appears on setUser — and nowhere else. It is never attached to an action.

learndash.note: Completions are form posts that reload the page, so they arrive from the server on the next page. Lesson video comes from the engagement kit, running alongside.

scenarios.label: A course, start to finish
scenarios.note: Enrol, finish two lessons and a topic, watch the lesson video, pass the quiz and finish the course. The quiz reports its score, never the answers.

scenarios.label: Completion page reloaded
scenarios.note: The completion page prints the same events again on a reload. Each has an ID the plugin already reported, so both are refused and nothing is counted twice.

scenarios.label: Cookie banner unanswered
scenarios.note: Without consent the learner is not identified and no learning event is sent. Each one is refused, with the reason.

onetrust.note: RUM is held until the analytics category is accepted.

scenarios.label: Walk the banner
scenarios.note: RUM is held until the analytics category is accepted, then released. Turning it back off withdraws consent.

scenarios.label: Require a stricter category
scenarios.note: Now only "accepts all cookies" releases RUM. Accepting analytics alone is not enough.
